```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
source("00_setup.R")

# Upstream requirement:
#   01_data_import_cleaning.Rmd -> Chik_total
# Chik_total is already the confirmed chikungunya analytic population.

STUDY_START_YEAR <- 2016L
STUDY_END_YEAR   <- 2025L
STUDY_START_DATE <- as.Date("2016-01-01")
STUDY_END_DATE   <- as.Date("2025-12-31")
STUDY_LABEL      <- "2016-2025"
FOLLOWUP_DAYS    <- 180L

stopifnot(
  exists("Chik_total"),
  all(Chik_total$CLASSI_FIN %in% c(1, 13)),
  all(as.Date(Chik_total$DT_SIN_PRI) >= STUDY_START_DATE),
  all(as.Date(Chik_total$DT_SIN_PRI) <= STUDY_END_DATE)
)

chik <- Chik_total %>%
  mutate(
    onset = as.Date(DT_SIN_PRI),
    hosp  = as.Date(DT_INTERNA),
    death = as.Date(DT_OBITO),
    end_fu = as.Date(DT_ENCERRA),
    # Force missing outcome indicators to FALSE so status never becomes NA.
    is_death = dplyr::coalesce(EVOLUCAO == 2, FALSE),
    is_hosp  = dplyr::coalesce(as.character(HOSPITALIZ) == "1", FALSE) & !is.na(hosp),
    age_group_surv10 = factor(
      as.character(age_group_surv10),
      levels = c("<1", "1-9", "10-19", "20-29", "30-39",
                 "40-49", "50-59", "60-69", "70-79", ">=80")
    ),
    sex = case_when(
      CS_SEXO == "F" ~ "Female",
      CS_SEXO == "M" ~ "Male",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    race5 = case_when(
      race_label %in% c("Asian", "Black", "Indigenous", "Pardo (Mixed)", "White") ~ race_label,
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    race5 = factor(
      race5,
      levels = c("Pardo (Mixed)", "White", "Black", "Asian", "Indigenous")
    )
  )
```

## Construct valid 180-day survival datasets

The original file clipped all event times above 180 days to day 180 while retaining
`status = 1`, which incorrectly converts later events into events at the administrative
censoring boundary. Here, events after 180 days are treated as censored at 180 days.
For onset-based intervals, closure/censoring time is measured from symptom onset;
for the hospitalization-to-death interval it is measured from hospital admission.

```{r survival-dataset-builder}
build_surv_dataset <- function(df, interval, horizon = FOLLOWUP_DAYS) {

  if (!interval %in% c("onset_to_hosp", "hosp_to_death", "onset_to_death")) {
    stop("Unknown interval: ", interval)
  }

  if (interval == "onset_to_hosp") {
    d <- df %>%
      mutate(
        event_day = as.numeric(hosp - onset),
        censor_day = as.numeric(end_fu - onset),
        event_recorded = is_hosp & !is.na(event_day) & event_day >= 0
      )
  }

  if (interval == "onset_to_death") {
    d <- df %>%
      mutate(
        event_day = as.numeric(death - onset),
        censor_day = as.numeric(end_fu - onset),
        event_recorded = is_death & !is.na(event_day) & event_day >= 0
      )
  }

  if (interval == "hosp_to_death") {
    d <- df %>%
      filter(is_hosp, !is.na(hosp)) %>%
      mutate(
        event_day = as.numeric(death - hosp),
        censor_day = as.numeric(end_fu - hosp),
        event_recorded = is_death & !is.na(event_day) & event_day >= 0
      )
  }

  d %>%
    mutate(
      # Negative closure intervals are invalid and cannot define censoring.
      censor_day = if_else(!is.na(censor_day) & censor_day >= 0,
                           censor_day, NA_real_),

      # An event must occur before the administrative horizon and, when a
      # closure date exists, no later than the recorded closure date.
      event_within_followup = event_recorded &
        event_day <= horizon &
        (is.na(censor_day) | event_day <= censor_day),

      status = as.integer(event_within_followup),

      # If an event is known to have occurred after 180 days, the record is
      # known to be event-free through day 180 even if closure is unavailable.
      known_beyond_horizon = event_recorded & event_day > horizon,

      t_obs = case_when(
        event_within_followup ~ event_day,
        known_beyond_horizon ~ as.numeric(horizon),
        !is.na(censor_day) ~ pmin(censor_day, as.numeric(horizon)),
        TRUE ~ NA_real_
      )
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(t_obs), t_obs >= 0, t_obs <= horizon)
}

intervals <- c("onset_to_hosp", "hosp_to_death", "onset_to_death")

surv_data <- setNames(
  lapply(intervals, function(x) build_surv_dataset(chik, x)),
  intervals
)

surv_audit <- bind_rows(lapply(names(surv_data), function(int_name) {
  d <- surv_data[[int_name]]
  tibble(
    interval = int_name,
    n = nrow(d),
    events_180d = sum(d$status, na.rm = TRUE),
    censored_180d = sum(d$status == 0L, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_followup_days = median(d$t_obs, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}))

print(surv_audit)
```

## Kaplan-Meier curves

```{r km-functions}
interval_labels <- c(
  onset_to_hosp  = "Symptom onset to hospitalization",
  hosp_to_death  = "Hospitalization to death",
  onset_to_death = "Symptom onset to death"
)

group_specs <- list(
  age = list(var = "age_group_surv10", ref = "20-29"),
  sex = list(var = "sex", ref = "Female"),
  race = list(var = "race5", ref = "Pardo (Mixed)")
)

prepare_group <- function(d, var, ref = NULL) {
  out <- d %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[var]]))
  out$grp <- factor(out[[var]])
  if (!is.null(ref) && ref %in% levels(out$grp)) {
    out$grp <- relevel(out$grp, ref = ref)
  }
  out
}

plot_km <- function(d, interval, group_name, horizon = FOLLOWUP_DAYS) {
  spec <- group_specs[[group_name]]
  dd <- prepare_group(d, spec$var, spec$ref)

  if (nrow(dd) < 10 || n_distinct(dd$grp) < 2) return(NULL)

  survfit2(Surv(t_obs, status) ~ grp, data = dd) |>
    ggsurvfit() +
    add_confidence_interval() +
    add_risktable(
      risktable_stats = c("{n.risk}", "{n.censor}"),
      risktable_height = 0.35
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, horizon)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
    labs(
      title = paste0(interval_labels[[interval]], " by ", group_name),
      subtitle = paste0("Confirmed chikungunya, Brazil, ", STUDY_LABEL,
                        "; administrative horizon = ", horizon, " days"),
      x = "Days",
      y = "Event-free survival probability",
      color = NULL
    )
}
```

```{r km-plots}
km_plots <- list()

for (int_name in intervals) {
  for (gname in names(group_specs)) {
    key <- paste(int_name, gname, sep = "__")
    p <- plot_km(surv_data[[int_name]], int_name, gname)
    km_plots[[key]] <- p
    if (!is.null(p)) print(p)
  }
}
```

## Log-rank tests

```{r log-rank-tests}
logrank_results <- list()

for (int_name in intervals) {
  for (gname in names(group_specs)) {
    spec <- group_specs[[gname]]
    d <- prepare_group(surv_data[[int_name]], spec$var, spec$ref)

    if (nrow(d) < 10 || n_distinct(d$grp) < 2) next

    lr <- survdiff(Surv(t_obs, status) ~ grp, data = d)
    p_val <- 1 - pchisq(lr$chisq, df = length(lr$n) - 1)

    key <- paste(int_name, gname, sep = "__")
    logrank_results[[key]] <- list(test = lr, p_value = p_val)

    cat("\n", key, "\n", sep = "")
    print(lr)
    cat("Log-rank p-value:", format.pval(p_val, digits = 3), "\n")
  }
}
```

## Univariable Cox models

Age uses 20-29 years as the explicit reference group, sex uses female as the
reference group, and race/ethnicity uses Pardo (Mixed) as the reference group.

```{r univariable-cox}
run_univariable_cox <- function(d, var, ref = NULL) {
  dd <- d %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(.data[[var]]),
      !is.na(status),
      !is.na(t_obs)
    )

  dd$grp <- factor(dd[[var]])
  if (!is.null(ref) && ref %in% levels(dd$grp)) {
    dd$grp <- relevel(dd$grp, ref = ref)
  }

  # x = TRUE is needed for cox.zph(), but the fitted Cox object can be very
  # large with ~1.2 million records. Compute the small summaries first, then
  # explicitly discard the full fit/design matrix before returning.
  fit <- coxph(
    Surv(t_obs, status) ~ grp,
    data = dd,
    ties = "efron",
    x = TRUE,
    model = FALSE,
    y = FALSE
  )

  tidy_res <- broom::tidy(fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
  ph_res <- cox.zph(fit)
  n_res <- nrow(dd)
  events_res <- sum(dd$status, na.rm = TRUE)

  rm(fit, dd)
  invisible(gc())

  list(
    tidy = tidy_res,
    ph = ph_res,
    n = n_res,
    events = events_res
  )
}

cox_univariable <- list()

for (int_name in intervals) {
  for (gname in names(group_specs)) {
    spec <- group_specs[[gname]]
    key <- paste(int_name, gname, sep = "__")

    res <- run_univariable_cox(
      surv_data[[int_name]],
      var = spec$var,
      ref = spec$ref
    )

    cox_univariable[[key]] <- res

    cat("\n==============================\n")
    cat(key, "| n =", res$n, "| events =", res$events, "\n")
    print(res$tidy)
    cat("\nProportional-hazards test:\n")
    print(res$ph)
  }
}
```

## Mutually adjusted Cox sensitivity models

These models jointly adjust for age group, sex, and race/ethnicity. They use a
common complete-case population within each survival interval, so their sample
sizes differ from the corresponding univariable analyses.

```{r adjusted-cox}
run_adjusted_cox <- function(d) {
  dd <- d %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(age_group_surv10),
      !is.na(sex),
      !is.na(race5),
      !is.na(status),
      !is.na(t_obs)
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      age_group_surv10 = relevel(factor(age_group_surv10), ref = "20-29"),
      sex = relevel(factor(sex), ref = "Female"),
      race5 = relevel(factor(race5), ref = "Pardo (Mixed)")
    )

  fit <- coxph(
    Surv(t_obs, status) ~ age_group_surv10 + sex + race5,
    data = dd,
    ties = "efron",
    x = TRUE,
    model = FALSE,
    y = FALSE
  )

  tidy_res <- broom::tidy(fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
  ph_res <- cox.zph(fit)
  n_res <- nrow(dd)
  events_res <- sum(dd$status, na.rm = TRUE)

  rm(fit, dd)
  invisible(gc())

  list(
    tidy = tidy_res,
    ph = ph_res,
    n = n_res,
    events = events_res
  )
}

# Run one interval at a time and retain only compact summaries. This avoids
# keeping several million-row Cox design matrices in memory simultaneously.
cox_adjusted <- list()
for (int_name in intervals) {
  cox_adjusted[[int_name]] <- run_adjusted_cox(surv_data[[int_name]])
  invisible(gc())
}

for (int_name in intervals) {
  res <- cox_adjusted[[int_name]]
  cat("\n==============================\n")
  cat("Adjusted model:", int_name, "| n =", res$n, "| events =", res$events, "\n")
  print(res$tidy)
  cat("\nProportional-hazards test:\n")
  print(res$ph)
}
```

## Age-specific death gradient for downstream severity analyses

This extracts the age coefficients from the primary univariable death models.
Hazard ratios are relative hazards, not absolute mortality risks; downstream
expected-burden calculations must not treat these HRs alone as probabilities.

```{r export-age-gradients}
age_hr_onset_death <- cox_univariable[["onset_to_death__age"]]$tidy %>%
  transmute(
    interval = "onset_to_death",
    term,
    HR = estimate,
    CI_low = conf.low,
    CI_high = conf.high,
    p_value = p.value
  )

age_hr_hosp_death <- cox_univariable[["hosp_to_death__age"]]$tidy %>%
  transmute(
    interval = "hosp_to_death",
    term,
    HR = estimate,
    CI_low = conf.low,
    CI_high = conf.high,
    p_value = p.value
  )

age_hr_export <- bind_rows(age_hr_onset_death, age_hr_hosp_death)
print(age_hr_export)
```

## Scope and internal-consistency checks

```{r scope-sanity}
cat("Study period:", STUDY_LABEL, "\n")
cat("Confirmed chikungunya cases:", nrow(chik), "\n")
cat("Recorded deaths:", sum(chik$is_death, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Recorded hospitalizations with admission date:", sum(chik$is_hosp, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

stopifnot(
  min(chik$onset, na.rm = TRUE) >= STUDY_START_DATE,
  max(chik$onset, na.rm = TRUE) <= STUDY_END_DATE,
  all(vapply(surv_data, function(x) all(x$t_obs >= 0 & x$t_obs <= FOLLOWUP_DAYS), logical(1))),
  all(vapply(surv_data, function(x) all(x$status %in% c(0L, 1L)), logical(1))),
  all(c("onset_to_hosp", "hosp_to_death", "onset_to_death") %in% names(cox_adjusted))
)
```
